name: What's the difference between a retail build-out and a tenant improvement?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a retail build-out and a tenant improvement?

acceptedAnswer.text: The terms 'retail build-out' and 'tenant improvement' are often used interchangeably, but there's a subtle distinction. A build-out typically refers to constructing a new space from a raw shell, or making significant structural changes to an existing one to suit a new retail tenant. Tenant improvements (TIs) generally encompass less extensive modifications made to an existing space to meet a tenant's needs, often funded partly by the landlord. Both aim to customize a commercial space for a business.
acceptedAnswer.description: A retail build-out usually means constructing a new space from a raw shell, while tenant improvements involve less extensive modifications to an existing space.
